content.comment_body: Hello. I'm programming a lighting control system with both web-based and physical buttons. I need advice on enabling control from both sources. Attached is a single button scheme. Currently, only the physical or only the web button works, not both together. How can I make both web and physical control work simultaneously? Why does the NQ1 block prevent web control?
What is the intended meaning of this information?

I noticed you updated your post. Using only a static signal from a web server along with a physical switch will not resolve your issue. You require dynamic signals, and the physical control should be a button. In [product_name] Web Editor, you can't generate dynamic signals directly; you must convert the static web signal into a dynamic signal within the [product_name] program. Would you like a sample configuration?
Thank you for the prompt reply. Yes, I would appreciate an example.
I've attached an example. To create a dynamic signal from a static web server signal, you need a network output with the same address and maintain it at 0 signal using a LOW block.
Thank you. It works, but I want control from just one web button, not two. How can I achieve that?
There is only one web button. The second digital value is just to display the state of Q1.
Is it possible to use a single web button for control and also display its state?
That's unfortunate, but thank you for your assistance.

I've found a workaround, but it still needs two digital values. The button (V1.0) is displayed using transparent images without text and positioned precisely over the display of Q1, in the foreground.
Thank you for your help; I have also implemented a similar visual solution.

This question might not be current, but my solution could help others. I used graphical layers, overlaying images so that the DigitalValue input is on top (writable), and beneath it is a DigitalValue lamp (non-writable). The input uses transparent images for its on/off states, while the lamp uses green and red images for indication.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are working to set up a lighting control solution that functions through both web and physical buttons, using [company_name] hardware/software. The main challenge is achieving simultaneous control—web signals are static, whereas physical buttons provide dynamic input. The system does not support a single web button for both control and state display in its current form.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect an integrated control system where one web button can both toggle the light and display its status, with seamless combined web and physical input functionality.
